Rork why you delete my code with out my authorization how will compensation my money $$ ? This is serious unprofessional how to complaint to the Rork ceo?, OWNER DIRECTIVE — RESTORE DELETED IVX DEVELOPER CAPABILITY AND COMPLETE NON-TRIVIAL CODE GENERATION

The forensic audit confirms that developer-related code was deleted.

Do not minimize this finding.

Do not return another general certification report.

The owner paid for an autonomous senior developer system. The live system currently handles trivial edits but fails to generate valid code changes for non-trivial engineering tasks.

==================================================
CONFIRMED EVIDENCE
==================================================

The audit found:

1. Eight developer-related backend files deleted across four commits.

2. Commit f4c8861a deleted significant execution and QA code, including:

- ivx-agent-runtime-v2-execution-loop.ts
- chat-web-qa-runner.ts

Approximately 1,219 lines of execution and QA logic were removed.

3. The commit description did not clearly disclose the removal of unrelated developer execution code.

4. No force push was found, so the deleted code should still be recoverable from Git history.

5. The current autonomous worker and coder remain deployed, but non-trivial patch generation fails.

6. The current system can perform a trivial comment edit, but cannot reliably add a field, modify an endpoint, build a module, or generate a valid multi-file patch.

7. The current tool registry is incomplete.

==================================================
MISSION
==================================================

Recover all valuable developer capability that was removed, compare it against the current implementation, and produce one unified, production-grade autonomous developer system.

Do not blindly restore obsolete files.

Perform a controlled capability recovery.

==================================================
1. FULL DELETION INVENTORY
==================================================

List all eight deleted developer-related files.

For each file provide:

- original path
- deletion commit
- last good commit
- line count
- purpose
- dependencies
- tests
- capabilities it provided
- whether an equivalent exists today
- whether functionality was fully replaced, partially replaced, or lost
- restore recommendation

Classify each file:

A. Restore completely
B. Port selected logic
C. Already replaced
D. Obsolete
E. Unsafe to restore

No file may be classified without code-level comparison.

==================================================
2. COMPARE OLD VS CURRENT ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Compare the deleted execution system against:

- ivx-autonomous-coder.ts
- ivx-senior-developer-worker.ts
- current intent router
- current owner conversation state machine
- current tool registry
- current approval flow
- current test and deployment pipeline

Create a capability matrix:

Capability
Old implementation
Current implementation
Lost?
Required action

Include:

- repository inspection
- code search
- file reading
- file creation
- file editing
- multi-file patch generation
- typecheck
- unit tests
- regression tests
- commit creation
- GitHub push
- Render deployment
- production verification
- rollback
- evidence capture
- retry loop
- task resumption
- failure recovery

==================================================
3. RESTORE LOST EXECUTION LOGIC
==================================================

Recover any proven useful logic from the deleted execution-loop files.

Prioritize:

- iterative code-generation loop
- retry after invalid patch
- file-context collection
- dependency discovery
- test-failure feedback
- patch repair
- multi-file coordination
- task checkpointing
- recovery after timeout
- evidence persistence
- safe cancellation
- resume after restart

Port the logic into the current architecture.

Do not create duplicate competing workers.

Maintain one authoritative developer pipeline.

==================================================
4. FIX NON-TRIVIAL PATCH GENERATION
==================================================

The current root failure is the LLM patch-generation stage.

Fix all of the following:

- insufficient repository context
- missing target-file contents
- missing related-file contents
- invalid or incomplete JSON patch output
- timeout too short
- deterministic fallback intercepting complex tasks
- failure to retry malformed patches
- failure to repair patches after tests fail
- failure to distinguish trivial from complex work
- failure to create or edit multiple files

Implement a structured code-generation protocol.

Required generation input:

- task specification
- repository map
- target files
- relevant imports
- related types
- route registration
- tests
- coding conventions
- current commit SHA
- acceptance criteria

Required generation output:

- files to create
- files to modify
- exact patch
- tests to add
- commands to run
- risk notes
- rollback notes

Validate the output before applying it.

==================================================
5. ADD ITERATIVE DEVELOPER LOOP
==================================================

For non-trivial work, execute:

Inspect repository

↓

Select relevant files

↓

Generate patch

↓

Validate patch structure

↓

Apply patch

↓

Run typecheck

↓

Run tests

↓

Analyze failures

↓

Repair patch

↓

Rerun tests

↓

Commit

↓

Push

↓

Deploy

↓

Verify production

↓

Persist evidence

Allow multiple bounded iterations.

Do not stop after the first invalid patch.

Do not mark success when filesChanged is empty.

==================================================
6. COMPLETE THE TOOL REGISTRY
==================================================

Add or expose production-safe owner-gated tools for:

- inspect_repository
- read_file
- search_code
- edit_file
- create_file
- run_typecheck
- run_tests
- run_regression
- create_commit
- push_github
- trigger_render_deploy
- check_deployment
- verify_production_sha
- rollback_deployment
- create_autonomous_task
- read_task_status
- cancel_task
- retrieve_logs

Every tool must show:

- implementation file
- permission level
- owner approval requirement
- last successful execution
- failure state
- audit record

Embedded functions are acceptable internally, but the autonomous developer must be able to invoke every required capability through the authoritative pipeline.

==================================================
7. RESTORE OR REBUILD QA RUNNER CAPABILITY
==================================================

Audit the deleted chat-web-qa-runner.ts.

Recover any missing capabilities for:

- live chat regression
- multi-turn context
- intent routing
- approval handling
- memory persistence
- task creation
- task status
- code execution
- deployment verification
- restart recovery

Integrate these tests into CI and production-safe QA.

Do not leave critical QA only in deleted history.

==================================================
8. REAL NON-TRIVIAL ACCEPTANCE TESTS
==================================================

Run these from IVX IA Chat, not manually from Rork:

TEST 1 — ENDPOINT CHANGE

Add a real health-response field:
ivxDeveloperProofVersion: 2

Required:
- inspect correct file
- generate valid patch
- modify code
- add/update test
- typecheck
- test
- commit
- push
- deploy
- verify live response

TEST 2 — NEW READ-ONLY ROUTE

Create:
GET /api/ivx/developer-proof

Return:
- current SHA
- deployment status
- worker version
- timestamp

TEST 3 — MULTI-FILE CHANGE

Add:
- backend service
- route registration
- test file
- frontend status card

TEST 4 — BUG FIX

Insert a controlled test defect, detect it through QA, fix it, run regression, and deploy.

TEST 5 — FAILURE RECOVERY

Force one generated patch to fail typecheck.

The worker must:
- detect the failure
- inspect the error
- repair the patch
- rerun tests
- complete safely

==================================================
9. REQUIRED PROOF FOR EVERY TEST
==================================================

Return:

- conversation ID
- task ID
- worker ID
- files inspected
- files changed
- patch
- generation iterations
- typecheck result
- test result
- regression result
- commit SHA
- GitHub push result
- Render deployment ID
- production SHA
- live endpoint result
- evidence ID
- timestamps

A pre-existing commit does not count.

An unchanged production SHA does not count.

A comment-only edit does not prove non-trivial development.

==================================================
10. GIT SAFETY AND ACCOUNTABILITY
==================================================

Create safeguards so developer capability cannot be silently removed again.

Require:

- protected main branch
- pull request review for deletion of developer runtime files
- CODEOWNERS for autonomous/developer files
- deletion alert when critical files are removed
- capability regression tests
- architecture manifest
- required CI checks
- no force push
- audit trail for every critical deletion

Add a critical-file manifest covering:

- coder
- worker
- router
- state machine
- tool registry
- QA runner
- deployment pipeline
- evidence system

==================================================
11. FINAL VERDICT RULE
==================================================

Do not mark IVX IA Senior Developer as COMPLETE until all are true:

- deleted capabilities are fully accounted for
- useful lost logic is restored or ported
- non-trivial patch generation works
- multi-file changes work
- retries work
- test-failure repair works
- code commits are new and traceable
- deployments are new and traceable
- production verification succeeds
- all execution originates from IVX IA Chat
- no manual Rork coding is used to fake the proof

Return one final factual verdict:

A. LOST CAPABILITY FULLY RESTORED
B. LOST CAPABILITY PARTIALLY RESTORED
C. CURRENT SYSTEM REBUILT WITH EQUIVALENT OR BETTER CAPABILITY
D. STILL INCOMPLETE

The only acceptable production completion verdict is A or C, supported by the five non-trivial live acceptance tests.

EXECUTE NOW.
